sources.claim: Tax is pay-as-you-go: people who do not have enough tax withheld, such as many self-employed people, may need to pay estimated tax in installments during the year.

sections.skill: Set aside a planned share of income for taxes

questions.prompt: With a 25 percent assumption, how much of a 1,200-dollar payment goes to tax savings?
questions.intro: Because taxes for the self-employed are not withheld, a simple habit is to move a set percentage of each payment into a separate tax savings account. The right percentage depends on your situation; this course uses percentages like 25 or 30 percent only as PRACTICE ASSUMPTIONS, not as advice. Example with a 25 percent assumption: a 2,000-dollar payment means moving 500 dollars to tax savings. Check the amount with a tax professional or IRS tools, and adjust when income changes.

sections.skill: Taking a share and keeping the rest

questions.prompt: Set aside 20 percent of 1,000. How much is set aside?
questions.intro: If you set aside a share of a payment, you keep the rest. Set aside = percent x payment; keep = payment - set aside. With 25 percent of 800: set aside 0.25 x 800 = 200, keep 800 - 200 = 600. Shortcut: keep = payment x (1 - percent) = 800 x 0.75 = 600. Check: 200 + 600 = 800. The two parts always add back to the full payment.
